title: India's forex reserves fall $2.69 billion to $717 billion, second weekly drop
dek: Foreign currency assets and gold both fell in the week to 30 October, leaving reserves about $69 billion below September's record.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $2.69 billion to $717.06 billion in the week ended 30 October, according to the Reserve Bank of India's weekly data released on Friday, as reported, the second weekly fall in a row.

Foreign currency assets, the largest part of the reserves, fell by $2.09 billion to $591.12 billion. Gold reserves dropped by $559 million to $102.59 billion, and special drawing rights with the International Monetary Fund fell by $47 million to $18.56 billion. India's reserve position with the IMF rose by $3 million to $4.79 billion. In the previous week the reserves had fallen by $1.27 billion to $719.75 billion.

The RBI did not give a reason for the fall. Analysts linked it to the central bank selling dollars to support the rupee and to the use of funds raised through a special deposit scheme for non-resident Indians, according to reports. Changes in the value of non-dollar currencies and gold also move the total from week to week.

The reserves remain about $69 billion below their record of $785.71 billion, set in the week ended 4 September, when banks raised a record $133 billion through a concessional currency swap window for foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits. The reserves cover the country's import bill and give the RBI room to calm sharp swings in the rupee. The next weekly figures are due on Friday, 13 November.
